cases.name: Melissa Elayne Campbell
cases.about: Her obituary said: "She was a caring and passionate woman, who enjoyed the outdoors, exercise, and laughing with her friends and family. She was a romantic who always saw the best in people. She worked hard to study her way through college, while raising her two daughters to become a Registered Nurse. She deeply cared for people and animals and cherished taking care of them. She loved playing with and teaching her children and grandson about all of the magic and beauty of the world."
cases.narrative:
Police received a hang-up 911 call a little after 4 a.m. but were unable to track the location since it was immediately disconnected, the sheriff’s office said in its statement. The dispatchers repeatedly tried to contact the caller, and on one of the calls, they heard what sounded like a “voice softly [saying] the word ‘help.’”

As the effort continued to trace the phone, police were able to learn from the owner of the number that he had loaned it to someone, according to the statement. After investigating several possible locations, police traced the phone to the Gnadenhutten home. A family member was at the scene and let police in before the bodies were found, per the statement.
